decisions.decision: Which paths does MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS trust on the Mac? (core G6, extras G10)
decisions.ruling: The value is $HOME/.config/mise, <projects_dir>/github.com and <projects_dir>/gitlab.com. The user chose these paths. No new macos.toml key. Only the sibling folders of projects_dir (backup, copilot, tmp) lose trust. A repository at github.com/<anyone>/<repo> still loads its mise config with no prompt, so the warning not to clone an untrusted repository there stays.
decisions.rejected: No trust path, with mise trust for each repository; a list of owners; a new macos.toml key.

decisions.decision: Does the Mac user config keep python.uv_venv_auto? (core G5)
decisions.ruling: Delete python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source" from macos/tools/python/tools.toml. uv creates the project environment at uv run. The user accepted this, because the user-level config does not create the venv. repo/tools/python/tools.toml keeps the setting, so a repository that adopts the python tool still opts in. This protects only outside the trusted paths of D1.
decisions.rejected: The value source, because a repository can still put its own .venv/bin on PATH; a change to repo/tools/python.

decisions.decision: Where does the prompt command of custom.submodule_status run git status? (core G8, core G10)
decisions.ruling: Only when the top folder of the repository is below $PROJECTS_DIR/github.com or $PROJECTS_DIR/gitlab.com. Add case "$top/" in "$PROJECTS_DIR"/github.com/*|"$PROJECTS_DIR"/gitlab.com/*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac && before git status. Outside those folders, for example in an extracted archive in Downloads, no git status runs and no mark shows. With PROJECTS_DIR unset, no git status runs. An archive extracted inside the two folders can still run code: accepted. git prints a real path, so a projects_dir with a symlink in its path loses the mark: accepted. This guard covers only custom.submodule_status. The git_status module of starship stays, and it can still run the filter driver of a repository in any folder, as git status by hand does: accepted. A projects_dir with a trailing slash also loses the mark: accepted.
decisions.rejected: Remove the module; a list of repositories; git status with safe options, which cannot stop a repository-level fsmonitor in every case.

decisions.decision: How do the brew alias and updateall find the fnox config? (core G9)
decisions.ruling: Pin the user config: brew = "fnox -c $HOME/.config/fnox/config.toml exec -P brew -- brew", and fnox -c "$HOME/.config/fnox/config.toml" exec --profile brew -- mise run upgrade:brew in updateall/_default. mise writes the alias in single quotes in zsh, bash and fish, so $HOME expands when the alias runs. K2 tests this. The alias needs no template.
decisions.rejected: A .tmpl with .env.HOME, because the rendered file then holds one fixed home; no pin.

decisions.decision: What happens to CONTEXT7_RUNNER and the context7 fnox profile? (core G9)
decisions.ruling: Delete both. The user removed context7 from vwf and uses the official plugin of Claude Desktop. Delete the CONTEXT7_RUNNER line of settings.json.tmpl and the [profiles.context7.secrets.CONTEXT7_API_KEY] table of the fnox config. Add [ "env", "CONTEXT7_RUNNER" ] to remove of .claude/settings.json in claude-cli/tools.toml, because a merge file keeps a deleted key unless remove names it. Keep the mcp__plugin_context7_context7__* allow lines. The context7 addon of stackgen in claude-plugins keeps ${CONTEXT7_RUNNER:-pnpm dlx}: out of scope, because no repository uses it today.
decisions.rejected: Pin the runner with fnox -c; keep the profile for later use.

decisions.decision: What does the sync do with the mode of ~/.ssh? (shells G13, G14)
decisions.ruling: When setup_sync handles a target below .ssh/, it makes sure once in each run that the folder $_SS_HOME/.ssh has mode 700, on a new folder and on an existing folder. The check uses the path in the home folder, not the real path of a linked file. If ~/.ssh is itself a link, the check reads and sets the mode of the target of the link. A real run sets the mode, reports it, and sets _SS_CHANGED. A dry run changes nothing, and it reports the change only for an existing folder with another mode. It reports nothing for a missing folder. When the mode is already 700, the sync prints nothing about the folder.
decisions.rejected: Only a new folder; a chmod in a task; a mode key in tools.toml for one folder.

decisions.decision: How does upgrade/tailscale find the keg? (extras G11)
decisions.ruling: keg="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v tailscale)")")")". readlink -l gives illegal option on this Mac, and readlink -f gives an absolute path, so the /opt/homebrew/bin/ prefix goes away. If keg does not match */Cellar/tailscale/*, the task prints a warning, skips the chown and continues the upgrade, because the service is already stopped and a chown of another folder is not safe.
decisions.rejected: brew --prefix tailscale, because the chown needs the versioned keg.

decisions.decision: Which gaps stay as they are, and why?
decisions.ruling: Accept these, with the reason of each in the table of 04-docs.md. extras G7 and apps G3: the user uses skip-permissions on purpose. extras G8: tailscale must run as root. apps G2: deliberate. extras G9: skip-permissions sessions do not use the allow list. extras G14: the bootstrap source owns the key, and the live file lacks it. apps G4 and G5: opt-in tools with chosen taps. entry-tool D16 and D17: the earlier rulings stand, and their gaps G5 and G6 are already closed. shells G8: accept-new is the normal tradeoff. shells G9: the pin rule exempts dev tooling. shells G10, G11 and G15: the attacker must already run as the user. shells G12: GitHub still shows the mode change, and a change shows mode differences in all repositories. front-end G5, G7 and G8 and extras G12 and G13: the values file is trusted, there is no privilege gain, and the design docs setup-sync.md and repo-sync.md hold the rules. core G7 and G10: spec gaps that D1 and D3 now answer.
decisions.rejected: Fix each one, which costs more than the risk on one user's Mac.

decisions.ruling: No. gaps_of sets a row to open 0 for all its gaps, and these folders also hold non-security gaps that stay open. U4 closes only the security entries, each with its ruling in its text. A1 recounts the 9 rows after landing. The row of macos-entry-tool does not change, because its security gaps are already closed.
decisions.rejected: gaps_of on the 5 folders, which hides the open non-security gaps.

decisions.decision: Where does the same fix for the live dotfiles land?
decisions.ruling: In a separate plan of the macos-setup repository, docs/plans/2026-11-06-dotfiles-security. One run works in one repository. This plan does not require it, and it does not edit macos-setup. macos-setup/tools/ does not change, because this repository replaces that copy.

decisions.decision: Is this a reversal of D4, D13 and D14 of the macos-tools plans, which copy values byte for byte?
decisions.ruling: No. Those rulings applied to the import. A security fix after the import is a new change. These value differences from macos-setup are the drift that the user approved, and the macos-setup plan brings the live dotfiles to the same values.
decisions.rejected: Treat it as a reversal with a decisions record.
